code_findings.title: When ChatGoogle.thinking_budget is explicitly set to any non-None value other than -1, ainvoke sends -1 rather than the selected value in the request config.
code_findings.explanation: The public dataclass field accepts an integer or None, but ainvoke only tests whether it is non-None and then writes the literal -1 instead of self.thinking_budget. That config is passed to generate_content. The change replaced the prior value-preserving expression with the literal -1, so it directly introduces this loss of caller configuration. Repository searches found no in-repository explicit caller, and the supplied evidence does not establish the Google SDK's behavioral semantics for -1, 0, or positive values; therefore no broader claim about actual latency, cost, or reasoning behavior is supported.
code_findings.impact: Caused by the change: Before the change, the dictionary used self.thinking_budget; the changed line instead unconditionally stores -1 whenever line 201's non-None condition succeeds. The resulting config is then supplied to generate_content, so an explicit value such as 0 or a positive integer cannot reach the generated request unchanged.

pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: The Google chat adapter adds Gemini 2.5 model identifiers, changes how thinking configuration is sent, delegates retries to the Google client instead of performing its own retry loop, broadens structured-response parsing to accept fenced JSON, and adds detailed timing/error logging. Actual user impact depends on which callers instantiate this adapter, their options, provider responses, and Google SDK behavior.

behavior_changes.description: Typed callers can now select three Gemini 2.5 model identifiers recognized by the adapter's verified-model annotation.
evidence: The verified model literal now includes Gemini 2.5 Flash, Flash Lite, and Pro identifiers.

behavior_changes.description: Invocations now default thinking_budget to 0, but every non-None value causes the provider request to receive a thinking budget of -1 rather than the configured value.
evidence: The field default is now non-None, so the thinking configuration branch is taken by default.
The request configuration uses the constant -1 instead of self.thinking_budget.

behavior_changes.description: The adapter no longer performs its own ten-attempt exponential retry loop; it makes the call once at this layer and relies on retry behavior provided by the Google client.
evidence: The manual retry loop was removed.
The remaining path explicitly delegates retry handling to the client before awaiting one helper invocation.

citations.quoted_text: # Let Google client handle retries internally with proper connection management

behavior_changes.description: When native structured output has no parsed object but returns JSON text enclosed in a complete Markdown code fence, the adapter now removes that fence before decoding and validating the JSON.
evidence: The native structured-output fallback normalizes response text and handles both json-labeled and unlabeled fences before json.loads.

behavior_changes.description: Google model calls now emit model-specific debug timing information and explicit warnings for empty text responses, changing operational observability without changing the returned empty-string fallback.
evidence: The invocation logs its start, elapsed response time, and empty response condition.

important_symbols.reason: It contains the externally visible request configuration, structured-output decoding, retry delegation, exception classification, and new diagnostics.
It defines which Google model identifiers typed callers and tooling regard as supported.
It establishes the model-specific logging namespace used by the new request, response, and failure diagnostics.

investigation_hints.description: Find all construction and configuration sites for ChatGoogle, especially callers setting thinking_budget or relying on its previous None default.
Inspect Google client creation and SDK retry configuration to determine the effective attempt count, backoff, timeout, and retryable-error policy after removal of the local loop.
Trace structured-output callers and the supports_structured_output decision to determine which models use native schema mode versus prompt-based JSON fallback.
Review cancellation propagation and exception translation across async callers, including whether callers expect task cancellation or a provider error.

local_risks.description: The configured thinking_budget is not preserved: all non-None values, including the new default and explicit caller values, collapse to -1. If callers use this option to enforce reasoning, latency, or cost constraints, the request can materially violate their selected configuration.

The enhanced cancellation diagnosis is inside an Exception handler while specifically testing asyncio.CancelledError. On Python runtimes where CancelledError is not an Exception subclass, actual task cancellation bypasses this logic, so the intended 504 diagnosis is not produced.
